title: Conveyor-oven sampling, jitter, and missed scans
equipment: Conveyor drying oven, product-zone temperature sensor, heater power stage, and belt-speed measurement
physicalPurpose: Hold product-zone temperature while proving how actual PLC execution timing changes a digital PI response and when timing must become a safe fault.
principalTechnique: Measured elapsed time with an explicit valid timing envelope
objective: Configure and validate measured elapsed time for a simulated conveyor-oven temperature loop; predict its effect on time-scaled PI calculations, compare equivalent fixed and jittered runs, and prove that a missed scan latches safe zero trim until reviewed reset and explicit automatic re-enable.

simplifications: The oven is one local FOPDT temperature-deviation model around 120 degC.
Belt speed remains 0.5 m/s so timing is the only changed quantity.
Spatial gradients, moisture dynamics, radiation, sensor filtering, scheduler causality, and pre-sampling aliasing sources are omitted.

baseline.limitation: A hard-coded nominal interval applies half the intended integral increment during a 200 ms scan.

change.decision: Pass measured elapsed time inside 0 < dt <= 250 ms; outside that envelope, latch the timing fault, do not update PID state, command zero trim, and require valid Manual reset plus separate automatic re-enable.

disturbances: Repeat at 50, 100, and 200 ms and with 20/180/50/150/100 ms deterministic timing
Request separate 300 ms and 0 ms fault cases
Restore valid timing, explicitly reset in Manual, then issue a separate automatic enable

acceptance.window: maximum absolute difference from Actual cycle time over complete run
sample-interval-weighted physical time 25.0 through 30.0 s after settling qualification
300 ms and 0 ms cases plus valid-but-latched state

abortPredicates: PV, MV, or elapsed time is nonfinite
elapsed time is nonpositive or exceeds 0.25 s
PV or MV leaves its hard limit
safety.restorationMode: Latched zero trim; valid timing and explicit reset in Manual followed by a separate automatic enable
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Simulation timing evidence does not authorise changing a production task period; physical changes require scheduler, topology, and process review plus immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain digital sampling limits, use measured elapsed time correctly, and reject missed or invalid scans safely.

learning.context: Measurement filtering cannot correct the fact that a PLC controller observes and updates a continuous oven only at discrete, imperfect intervals.
learning.reason: Integral, derivative, rate-limit, and model updates all depend on elapsed time; nominal timing is wrong under jitter, while unbounded elapsed time is unsafe.
theory: Sampling observes a continuous signal at discrete times and a zero-order hold keeps MV constant between updates, adding effective delay.
Sampling frequency is 1/dt and Nyquist frequency is half of it; content above Nyquist aliases and measured-dt arithmetic cannot restore it.
PI integral increment is Ki times error times dt, numerical derivative divides a sample difference by dt, and a rate limit permits rate times dt movement.
Measured dt preserves time scaling only inside a positive reviewed envelope; a missed scan must become an explicit fault rather than an ordinary update.
learning.workedPrediction: For Ki=0.667 %/(degC*s) and 1 degC error, first integral increments are 0.03335%, 0.0667%, and 0.1334% at 50, 100, and 200 ms; a nominal 100 ms value during a real 200 ms scan applies only half the intended increment.
practicalPreparation: Inspect the oven, sensor, power stage, belt speed, timing mode, actual/controller dt, validity, signals, units, limits, and safe state.
Calculate integral increments, sampling and Nyquist frequencies, and any rate-times-dt movement before running fresh equivalent cases.
learning.baseline: Run a 200 ms actual scan while the controller deliberately uses nominal 100 ms and retain the incorrect 0.0667-percentage-point first contribution as ineligible counter-evidence.
learning.change: Use measured elapsed time for 50, 100, and 200 ms and deterministic jitter, then prove latched zero, valid Manual reset, and separate automatic re-enable after invalid 300 and 0 ms cases.
learning.comparison: Compare first increments, equal-duration SP/PV/MV traces, timing traces, overshoot, settling, final error, bounds, and fault state without changing plant or gains.
learning.validation: Require exact calculated contributions, zero timing-use error in measured mode, qualified fixed and jittered responses, and a latched zero-output fault with reviewed reset and separate automatic re-enable outside 0 < dt <= 0.25 s.
learning.explanation: Measured dt preserves time-scaled arithmetic but does not make slow sampling equivalent to fast sampling or remove hold delay and aliasing.
learning.transfer: For another loop, obtain real timestamps, identify every time-scaled calculation, calculate sampling limits, define a maximum safe interval, compare equal experiments, and prove deterministic fault behavior.
